title: Check if Number is a Sum of Powers of Three
statement: A power of three is any number of the form `3^x` for an integer `x >= 0` (so `1, 3, 9, 27, ...`). Given the integer `n`, decide whether `n` equals the total of some collection of powers of three in which no power appears more than once. Return `true` if such a collection exists and `false` if it does not.
notes:
## Intuition

Every positive integer has exactly one base-3 representation, with digits 0, 1 and 2. Picking a set of distinct powers of three is the same as writing a base-3 number whose digits are only 0 or 1: digit 1 means "this power is used". So `n` works exactly when its base-3 digits contain no 2. (Trying every subset of the at most 15 relevant powers also works, but the digit view is direct.)

## Approach

1. While `n` is still positive, look at its lowest base-3 digit, `n % 3`.
2. If that digit is 2, the same power would be needed twice, so return `false`.
3. Otherwise drop the digit with `n = Math.floor(n / 3)` and continue.
4. If every digit was 0 or 1, return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 12`:

- `12 % 3 = 0`, so 3^0 is not used; `n` becomes 4.
- `4 % 3 = 1`, so 3^1 is used; `n` becomes 1.
- `1 % 3 = 1`, so 3^2 is used; `n` becomes 0.

No digit was 2, so the answer is `true` (12 = 3 + 9).

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n): each step removes one base-3 digit, at most 15 steps for `n <= 10^7`.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Use integer division (`Math.floor`) in JavaScript; `n / 3` alone leaves a fraction and the loop misbehaves.
- A digit 2 cannot be "fixed" by borrowing a larger power: `2 · 3^k = 3^(k+1) - 3^k` needs a subtraction, which the problem does not allow.
- Check every digit, not just the low ones: 18 is `200` in base 3, so its two lowest digits are 0 and the 2 only appears in the top digit.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | the part of the number whose base-3 digits are still unchecked |
| `n % 3` | the current lowest base-3 digit |

narration.2: Keep reading base-3 digits until none are left.
narration.3: The lowest base-3 digit of n is n % 3; a 2 would need the same power twice.
narration.4: Two copies of one power are not allowed, so n cannot be built.
narration.6: Remove the digit just checked by dividing by 3 and dropping the remainder.
narration.8: Every digit was 0 or 1, so the 1-digits name a valid set of distinct powers.
